s1.syndrome_frame: A syndrome of severe fatigue, muscular weakness, and cachexia with a large tumor on the distal part of the finger, associated with hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone levels
salient_findings: Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
Hypercalcemia and hypophosphatemia with elevated parathyroid hormone levels
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
History of primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation
Patient refused therapeutic management for primary hyperparathyroidism
Patient is cachectic
Significant muscular weakness
Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
Tumor has gradually enlarged in recent months
Hypercalcemia at 3.6 mmol/L
Hypophosphatemia at 0.65 mmol/L
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption
Chest radiograph revealed important deformation of the ribs
Thoracic CT scan revealed multiple lesions associated with multiple rib and vertebral fractures
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance

shortlist.label: Brown tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the histopathology of the finger tumor and is associated with hyperparathyroidism

shortlist.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism and current laboratory tests show elevated parathyroid hormone levels

shortlist.label: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism and a tumor on the distal part of the finger, which could be related to this syndrome

shortlist.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone levels, which are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: The histopathology of the finger tumor shows giant cells, which is consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated serum parathyroid hormone, combined with the presence of a tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger showing fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells with multiple osteoclast-like nuclei, are consistent with a brown tumor, which is a bone lesion associated with hyperparathyroidism.

rejected.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism, this is not a tumor diagnosis, but rather a condition that can cause brown tumors.

rejected.label: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome is characterized by a combination of hyperparathyroidism, jaw tumors, and other features, but the patient's presentation does not specifically suggest this syndrome.

rejected.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
rejected.why: This condition is a skeletal manifestation of hyperparathyroidism, but it is not a specific tumor diagnosis and does not fully explain the patient's tumor on the finger.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: While the tumor on the patient's finger contains giant cells, the overall clinical and histological picture is more consistent with a brown tumor, which is a specific type of bone lesion associated with hyperparathyroidism.
